question.problem: Find the remainder of the division $\frac{-3{x}^{4}+7{x}^{3}-4{x}^{2}-x+7}{x-2}.$
question.worked_solution:
Let $p(x)=-3{x}^{4}+7{x}^{3}-4{x}^{2}-x+7.$ 

The remainder theorem states that when $p(x)$ is divided by $(x-2),$ the remainder equals $p(2).$ 

Evaluating $p(2)$ directly gives

$$
\begin{aligned}p(2) & =-3(2)^{4}+7(2)^{3}-4(2)^{2}-2+7 \\  & =-48+56-16-2+7 \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

So, when $p(x)$ is divided by $(x-2),$ the remainder is $-3.$

**Note:** We can check the answer by carrying out synthetic division:

|  | ${x}^{4}$ | ${x}^{3}$ | ${x}^{2}$ | ${x}^{1}$ | ${x}^{0}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $2$ | $-3$ | $7$ | $-4$ | $-1$ | $7$ |
|  | $↓$ | $-6$ | $2$ | $-4$ | $-10$ |
|  | $-3$ | $1$ | $-2$ | $-5$ | $-3$ |
